players.description: MongoDB ObjectId referencing the country record from the countries collection. Identifies the player registered country.
Unique human-readable identifier given to the player. Used for login and player identification across the system.
Three-letter ISO currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, INR) defining the players wallet currency used for deposits, withdrawals, and gameplay.
Unique cryptographic token generated for the player to authenticate game sessions with integrated game providers.
Total monetary balance available in the players account, calculated as the sum of real, bonus, and any winnings-related balances.
Amount of real, withdrawable money available in the players wallet.
Amount of bonus funds received through promotions or rewards, subject to wagering rules.
Cumulative amount of all successful deposits made by the player across their account lifetime.
Cumulative amount of all completed withdrawals performed by the player.
Total amount currently under withdrawal processing or pending approval.
Total value of bonus money credited to the player.
Sum of all wager amounts placed using real funds.
Total winnings earned from bets placed with real balance.
Sum of all wager amounts placed using bonus funds.
Total winnings earned from bets placed with bonus balance.
Number of successful deposit transactions performed by the player.
Number of successful withdrawal transactions completed by the player.
Count of individual bets placed using real money.
Count of winning outcomes obtained from real-money bets.
Number of bets placed using bonus funds.
Number of winning outcomes obtained from bonus bets.
Timestamp indicating when the player last made a successful deposit.
Timestamp indicating when the player last completed a withdrawal.
Unique email address used for authentication, communication, and account recovery.
Boolean value indicating whether the player has verified their email through the verification process.
Indicates if the player has linked an external cryptocurrency wallet to their account.
Timestamp representing when the player profile was initially created.
Timestamp representing the most recent update to the players document.
Overall account status: Pending, Active, Inactive, or Fraud.
Indicates whether the player is eligible to receive bonus rewards. Can be enabled or disabled.
Controls whether marketing or system emails are enabled for the player.
Controls whether SMS notifications are enabled for the player.
Language preference code for user interface localization, using standard international language codes.
Securely hashed password string for login authentication.
Random cryptographic salt used to hash the players password.
Players phone number used for communication, verification, and security notifications.
Players personal first name.
Players personal surname or family name.
Gender identity of the player, used for demographic segmentation.
Players date of birth, used for age verification and responsible gaming checks.
Primary residential address provided by the player.
Secondary address line for additional address details.
State or province of the players registered address.
City of the players registered address.
Postal or ZIP code of the players address.
Token generated for password reset workflow, used once per reset attempt.
Metadata about the players last login session, such as IP address,loginAt, userAgent, or timestamp.
Indicates whether responsible gaming deposit limit rules are active for this player.
Monetary limit imposed on how much the player can deposit within a specific timeframe.
Interval for deposit limit enforcement (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, etc.).
Indicates whether bonus usage limits are enforced for this player.
Maximum amount of bonus funds the player is allowed to receive or use within a specified timeframe.
Frequency interval for evaluating the players bonus limit.
Defines which balance types the player can use during gameplay: Real, Bonus, or All.
Total loyalty reward points accumulated by the player from gameplay or promotions.
Numeric identifier of the players loyalty tier level.
Readable name of the players loyalty tier (e.g., Silver, Gold, Platinum).
ObjectId referencing the affiliate who referred the player, from the affiliates collection.
ObjectId referencing the specific affiliate marketing channel that generated the player signup.
Raw tracking parameters captured during registration for affiliate attribution.
Reference to the player categorization or segmentation profile used for behavior analysis.
URL pointing to the uploaded identity document used for KYC verification.
URL pointing to the players selfie or live image captured for KYC identity validation.
URL pointing to the uploaded utility bill or address proof document for KYC verification.
Current verification status of the uploaded identity document (Pending, Approved, Rejected).
Verification status of the uploaded selfie or face capture document.
Verification status of the uploaded address proof document.
Comments or notes added by compliance/KYC officers during document review.
Overall KYC compliance status of the player (Pending, Approved, Rejected, Expired, NoKyc).
Timestamp marking when the players KYC verification was approved.
Primary MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the player record.
Internal document version number maintained by Mongoose for schema migrations.

countries.description: Official country name used for player registration, regional configuration, and localization settings.
Operational status of the country within the platform. Determines whether the country is allowed for registration and gameplay. Values: Pending, Active, Inactive.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, INR) representing the countrys primary monetary unit used for player transactions.
Full name of the national currency used in the country, such as USD or Euro.
Symbol representing the countrys currency (e.g., $, €, ₹), used for UI display and financial formatting.
Name of the capital city of the country, useful for metadata, location-based segmentation, or informational reference.
Primary spoken language of the country in full language name form, used for localization defaults and culturally relevant content.
Two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., US, IN, GB) used for compliance validation, geographic routing, and UI localization.
Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country in extended format for standardized integrations.
Numeric ISO 3166 country code or standardized ISO identifier used in integrations and global data mappings.
Short language code (e.g., en, fr, de, zh-CN) representing the default language for users from this country. Mapped to i18n system language codes.
International dialing prefix assigned to the country (e.g., +1, +44, +91), used for mobile number validation and formatting.
Unicode emoji representing the country national flag, used for user interface display and visual selection inputs.
Direct URL pointing to the country flag image asset used in administrative dashboards or client UI applications.
Primary timezone identifier for the country (e.g., Asia/Kolkata, Europe/Paris), used for date-time normalization and user activity interpretation.
List of all supported timezone identifiers associated with the country, useful for countries spanning multiple zones.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the country record in the countries collection.
Internal version number maintained by Mongoose for tracking schema revisions and document updates.

transactions.description: MongoDB ObjectId referencing the country record from the countries collection. Identifies the player registered country.
Reference to the Country entity representing the player's registered geographical location.
Reference to the master provider or gaming vendor associated with the transaction, primarily used for game transactions.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the game record from the games collection. Used in bet, win, rollback and gameplay-related reporting.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing to Payment Gateway record from the paymentGateways collection. responsible for processing deposit or withdrawal operations.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the Audit record from the audits collection, enabling compliance validation and reconciliation tracking.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the Coupon record from the coupons collection, identifying the promotional voucher applied to the transaction.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the Affiliate record from the affiliates collection, used for partner performance and revenue attribution.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the AffiliateChannel record from the affiliateChannels collection, identifying the referral source that brought the player.
Indicates the method used for payment processing such as Visa, MasteCard, Crypto, etc.
Additional payment source identifier describing the intermediate service or processing route.
Wallet address used for cryptocurrency deposit or withdrawal processing.
Blockchain network used for crypto payments (e.g., TRC20, ERC20, BEP20).
Masked representation of the card used for the transaction, storing only the last four digits for security.
Date and time when the transaction event occurred, recorded in ISO format.
Unique identifier representing the transaction within the platform.
Defines the origin of the transaction such as Payment, Game, Admin, Affiliate, Kiosk, or Coupon operations.
Classifies the financial action involved: Deposit, Withdraw, Bet, Win, Credit, Debit, or Rollback.
Specifies whether the amount is Real, Bonus, or Mixed (Real_Bonus) balance.
Current processing state of the transaction such as Pending, Success, Failed, Cancelled, Refunded, or Chargeback.
Monetary amount involved in the transaction, representing value credited or debited.
Name or identifier of any bonus promotion associated with the transaction.
Final available real-money balance after processing the transaction.
Final available bonus balance after processing the transaction.
Currency code representing the player's default wallet configuration (e.g., USD, EUR, INR).
Balance representing accumulated winnings after the transaction.
Transaction value converted to system base currency which is EUR for analytics and reporting.
Currency used for deposit when different from player's default currency.
Amount received in the original deposit currency before conversion.
Raw transaction metadata or provider response stored for audit or debugging.
Free-text remarks describing additional transaction details or administrative comments.
Breakdown of amount distributed across multiple balances such as Real and Bonus funds.
Description of failure reason in case the transaction is rejected or unsuccessful.
IP address recorded at the time of the transaction, for security and fraud prevention.
Device type or user agent string representing the hardware used during the transaction.
Reference to the original transaction being reversed in case of rollback.
Reference to the deposit transaction related to subsequent bonus or credit rewards.
Original stake or wager amount associated with the winning outcome.
Boolean flag indicating whether this transaction represents the player’s first-ever deposit (First Time Deposit - FTD). Used for milestone tracking, promotional rewards, and affiliate attribution.

Boolean flag marking whether the player qualifies as a 'Qualified First Time Depositor' (QFTD). This identifies genuine depositors who continue to play or engage beyond the first deposit, as opposed to users who make a single deposit and churn. Commonly used for affiliate deal validation and revenue-sharing qualification.
Primary MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the transaction document.
Document version key maintained internally by Mongoose.

paymentGateways.description: Human-readable name of the payment gateway, displayed in dashboards and transaction processing modules.

Processor identifier used to route payments through the correct integration service. Possible values: CapitalManagement, GateCharge, GumBallPay, UZOpay, PayTechno, QuantumPay, Payofix, BlockBee, SmilePayz, Pragmatic, BlockSystems, EzzyGate, FreedomPay, Slikair, Paysecure, Superbit, Cash, Neosurf, Paysafe, Finvert, Paydot, Paympire, AstroPay, KwidPay, PayPound.
Defines the category of depositors supported by this gateway. Possible values: FTD (first-time depositors) and Recurring Depositors.
Operational status of the payment gateway. Determines whether it can be used by players. Values: Pending, Active, Inactive.
Array of payment methods offered by the gateway. Each method specifies currencies, countries, crypto support, and fees.
Name of the individual payment method (e.g., Visa, MasterCard, BTC, USDT).
Boolean indicating whether the method supports all platform currencies.
List of allowed currency codes for this method if not supporting all currencies.
Boolean indicating if the method supports cryptocurrency payments.
List of blockchain networks supported for crypto payments (e.g., ERC20, TRC20, BEP20).
Boolean indicating whether the method is available in all countries.
Array of MongoDB ObjectIds referencing Country collection. Specifies which countries are allowed to use this method.
Array of MongoDB ObjectIds referencing Country collection. Specifies countries blocked from using this method.
Percentage fee applied to successful transactions, used for settlement and accounting.
Fixed transaction fee applied per transaction regardless of transaction amount.
Fee applied when a refund is processed for this method.
Fee applied when a chargeback occurs for this method.
Percentage of settlement funds held temporarily as a reserve to cover potential chargebacks or disputes.
Number of days after which rolling reserve funds are released back to the settlement account.
Timestamp when the payment gateway record was created.
Timestamp representing the last update to the payment gateway record.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the payment gateway record in the PaymentGateways collection.
Internal Mongoose version key for concurrency control and document versioning.

playerCategorizations.description: Human-readable name of the player category (e.g., 'VIP', 'High Roller', 'Newcomer'). Used to label and segment players based on predefined criteria.
Internal level or tier identifier for the category, used to rank or prioritize categories hierarchically within the platform.
Hex code or color name representing the category visually in dashboards or UI displays for easy identification.
Count of players currently assigned to this category. Automatically updated as players qualify or exit the category.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the player categorization record in the PlayerCategorization collection.
Timestamp when the player categorization was created.
Timestamp of the last update to the player categorization record.
Internal Mongoose version key used for document versioning and concurrency control.

providers.description: Official name of the provider, used for identification across the platform and visible in dashboards or game listings.
Unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to the provider for internal referencing and integration purposes.
Default royalty or revenue share percentage allocated to the provider from transactions, bets, or game revenue.
Operational status of the provider within the platform. Values: Pending, Active, Inactive. Determines availability of games or services from this provider.
Timestamp when the provider record was created.
Timestamp of the last update to the provider record.
Preferred icon theme for the provider interface: Light, Dark, or Custom. Determines which icon variant is shown in the UI.
URL pointing to the provider's light-themed icon, used when UI theme is set to light.
URL pointing to the provider's dark-themed icon, used when UI theme is set to dark.
URL pointing to the provider's custom-themed icon, used if a custom branding theme is applied.
Hex code or CSS color used for provider branding backgrounds in dashboards or game interfaces.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the provider record in the Providers collection.
Internal Mongoose version key used for document versioning and concurrency control.

tournaments.description: Official name of the tournament, used for display in dashboards, player interfaces, and reporting.
Date and time when the tournament begins. Used to control player participation and scheduling.
Date and time when the tournament ends. Determines when results are finalized and prizes are distributed.
Operational status of the tournament. Values: Pending, Active, Inactive. Determines visibility and eligibility for players.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the Category record in categories collection that classifies the tournament (e.g., game type or event type).
Type of tournament based on player activity: Deposit, Bet, or Win. Defines how points or scores are calculated.
Detailed description of the tournament rules, rewards, and conditions for player participation.
Conversion ratio between wagers (bets/deposits) and tournament points. Used to calculate leaderboard standings.
Array of prize objects specifying rank-based rewards. Each prize includes rank, amount, and its unique MongoDB _id.
URL pointing to the tournament banner or image, used in UI dashboards and promotional materials.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the tournament record in the Tournaments collection.
Timestamp of the last update to the tournament record.
Timestamp when the tournament record was created.
Internal Mongoose version key used for document versioning and concurrency control.

games.description: MongoDB ObjectId referencing the master provider that owns or manages this game globally across multiple providers.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the Provider record for this specific game instance. Defines which provider supplies the game content.
Array of MongoDB ObjectIds referencing Category records. Used to classify the game into categories such as Slots, Live Casino, Table Games, Sports, etc.
Human-readable title of the game as displayed to players on UI and dashboards.
Internal remarks or operational notes about the game for administrative usage, invisible to players.
Current operational availability of the game. Values: Pending, Active, Inactive. Determines player access and visibility.
URL used to launch the game client. Accessed by operators or players when gameplay is initiated.
URL for the game thumbnail or banner used in frontend display such as lobbies and recommendations.
Boolean value indicating whether an image is available for the game. Used for fallback display handling.
Timestamp representing the creation date of the game record.
Timestamp representing the last time the game record was updated.
Date value used for sorting and prioritizing games based on relevance or recent updates.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the game in the Games collection.
Mongoose internal version key used to maintain document revision history and locking.

categories.description: Display name of the category (e.g., Slots, Roulette, Top Games). Used for UI grouping, filtering, and reporting.
Sorting order used to arrange categories visually in dashboards and gaming interfaces. Lower values appear first.
Operational state of the category. Values: Pending, Active, Inactive. Determines whether games under this category are displayed or hidden.
List of MongoDB ObjectIds referencing Provider records associated with this category. Defines which providers contribute games to the category.
Timestamp marking when the category was initially created in the system.
Timestamp of the most recent modification to the category record.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the category within the Categories collection.
Internal Mongoose version key used for document versioning and concurrency control.

communications.description: MongoDB ObjectId referencing another Communication record in the same collection when this message is part of a campaign chain.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the Player to whom the communication is addressed.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing the master/admin account that triggered or owns the communication.
Medium used for sending the communication. Allowed values: Mail or SMS.
State of the communication process. Possible values: Initiated, Success, or Failed.
Boolean indicating whether the communication is part of a promotional campaign or an individual message.
Array of recipient identifiers or contact values that the communication is sent to (e.g., email addresses or phone numbers).
Email address to which the message is sent, if communication type is Mail.
Phone number to which the message is sent, if communication type is SMS.
Title or subject line of the email or SMS message, used primarily for email communications.
Actual body text of the message delivered to the recipient(s).
Timestamp when the communication was dispatched to the messaging provider.
Response returned from the email/SMS provider after sending, typically used for delivery validation.
Error message logged if sending fails, used for debugging and reporting.
MongoDB ObjectId referencing EmailCredential to determine which email configuration was used for sending.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the communication record.
Mongoose internal version key for concurrency control and update tracking.

emailCredentials.description: Hostname or SMTP server address used for sending outbound emails (e.g., smtp.gmail.com, smtp.sendgrid.net).
Port number used for SMTP communication. Common values include 465 for SSL and 587 for TLS.
Current operational state of the email configuration. Values: Pending, Active, Inactive.
Boolean that determines whether TLS encryption is enabled for secure email transmission. Defaults to false.
Display name shown as the sender when recipients receive the email (e.g., Casino Support).
Email address used as the sending origin for outbound messages.
Password or API key used for authentication with the SMTP mail server.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the EmailCredential record.
Timestamp indicating when the email credential record was last modified.
Timestamp marking when the email credential record was initially created.
Mongoose internal version key used for document versioning and conflict resolution.

emailTemplates.description: Display name used to identify the email template within admin dashboards and configuration screens.
HTML markup that defines the body of the email template, including placeholders for dynamic values.
Specifies whether the template is automatic system-generated (Automate) or custom-created by an admin (Custom). Default is Custom.
Indicates the automated email event type when type is Automate. Examples: Player_Register, Forgot_Password, Deposit_Success, Withdraw_Request.
MongoDB ObjectId uniquely identifying the email template record.
Timestamp representing the last modification to the email template.
Timestamp marking when the email template record was initially created.
Mongoose internal version number used for concurrency control.
